findings.reasoning: The regulatory requirement (UCM § 1.10.3) mandates that water quality features maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outermost conductor of overhead distribution lines. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant; the absence of clearance documentation or calculations prevents confirmation that this requirement is met. This constitutes insufficient documentation rather than definitive non-compliance, warranting an 'unclear' status pending clarification.

The plans do not show any overhead distribution lines in the vicinity of the pond, nor do they provide clearance calculations demonstrating the required 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. Without profile views, engineer-sealed clearance documentation, or explicit callouts showing conductor locations relative to the pond, the specific clearance cannot be verified from available evidence. This is marked 'unclear' rather than 'fail' because the overhead line may be distant enough to comply, but documentation is insufficient to confirm compliance.

findings.observation: Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations) and Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) present detailed engineering information for the pond system. Sheet 16 contains cross-sectional profiles ('Pond Section A-A', 'Pond Section B-B', and 'Pond Outfall Detail') showing pond infrastructure, retaining walls, pipe routing, and elevation data. However, examination of these profile sheets reveals: (1) No overhead electric lines, conductors, or poles are depicted in any section view; (2) No clearance dimensions, measurements, or distance callouts between the pond and electric facilities are shown; (3) No professional engineer seal or notation indicating clearance verification for electric conductors; (4) The standard utility disclaimer note at the bottom states utilities 'may not match locations as constructed' but provides no affirmative clearance verification. The profiles show only pond construction details without reference to or coordination with the overhead electric line shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires profile plans and engineer-sealed section exhibits showing clearance verification between water quality features and all phases of overhead electric conductors and poles. The deficiency definition specifies 'missing required profile plans, engineer-scaled section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification and dimensions.' The pond profile sheets on Sheet 16 contain no overhead electric conductors or clearance dimensions—these sheets address only stormwater construction details. The regulatory requirement mandates that such clearance documentation exist and be provided; its complete absence constitutes a clear deficiency. The engineer must provide professionally-sealed profile or section views that explicitly depict the overhead electric facilities and demonstrate through dimensions and calculations that required clearances are maintained.

The absence of specific profile documentation showing vertical clearances between electrical equipment and the biofiltration-detention pond represents a potential gap in required design documentation.

findings.comment: Biofiltration/detention pond with retaining wall proposed immediately adjacent to northeast corner transmission easement; no documentation that pond design preserves Austin Energy access and maintenance vehicle turnaround requirements.
applicableAreas: Northeast corner of site, biofiltration/detention pond area adjacent to transmission easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a 'Biofiltration/Detention Pond' located in the northeast corner of the site, immediately adjacent to the north property line where a 5-foot electric easement and a 15-foot drainage easement/electric easement are located. Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan) and Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) detail the pond design and dimensions. The pond perimeter and retaining wall are shown immediately adjacent to the property boundary where the transmission easement is located. The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 16) explicitly prohibit: 'any structures, including but not limited to...drainage, filtration or detention ponds which would impair Austin Energy's access to the transmission easements or its lines, poles, structures, towers or appurtenant facilities in the easements.' The site plan does not provide documentation that the pond design has been reviewed for impact on transmission facility access or that the pond can be maintained while preserving Austin Energy's turnaround and maintenance vehicle access requirements.
findings.reasoning: While water quality features (detention ponds) may be allowable outside transmission easements with appropriate setbacks, the proposed pond's immediate adjacency to the transmission easement boundary raises questions about whether it impairs Austin Energy access as prohibited. The Electric Transmission Notes require that features not impair access, and the transmission facility access requirements (including 25-foot clearance from structure base for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles) must be verified. The site plan does not contain documentation that Austin Energy has reviewed and approved the pond location relative to access and maintenance requirements. The proximity of the pond with retaining wall immediately at the easement boundary creates uncertainty about whether the design preserves required access.

However, based on available evidence, there does not appear to be overhead distribution poles in close proximity to the pond.

findings.comment: The biofiltration/detention pond, including its retaining walls and required vegetation, is located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be relocated outside the easement boundary. Detention ponds cannot be located within electric easements as they obstruct required access and maintenance corridors.
applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond in northeastern corner within 5' Electric Easement
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 explicitly confirmed: 'Yes, the Biofiltration/Detention Pond overlaps. The eastern edge of the "Concrete Retaining Wall" enclosing the pond is drawn completely within the 5-foot space between the dashed easement line and the eastern property line.' Sheet 2 (Plat) shows 5' Electric Easements along property boundaries. Sheets 15-16 detail the detention pond structure and vegetation requirements. The drainage easements shown on Sheet 9 are separate from the electric easements. The detention pond itself, with its retaining walls, biofiltration media, and required vegetation, is located within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern boundary. This violates the principle that electric easements are reserved exclusively for electric facilities.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4 and § 1.14.7 specify that drainage structures, detention ponds, and other non-electric features are prohibited within electric easements where they would impair Austin Energy's access and maintenance of electric facilities. The submitted plans clearly show the detention pond retaining wall within the 5' electric easement. A detention pond with retaining walls, vegetation, and maintenance requirements is a drainage structure that obstructs the easement and prevents unobstructed access for electric facility maintenance.

findings.comment: Biofiltration/detention pond in the northeast corner is adjacent to overhead distribution electric line on eastern property boundary. No engineer-sealed profile or section exhibits demonstrate the required minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductors to pond edge. applicableAreas: Detention pond in northeast corner adjacent to overhead electric line on eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeast corner of the site adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) confirms an overhead electric line labeled '-OE-' running north-south along the eastern property boundary, positioned directly adjacent to the pond wall. Sheet 15 shows the pond plan details with rim elevation 681.00' and water surface elevations ranging from 676.25' to 676.75' for various storm events. Sheet 16 shows pond section profiles with detailed elevations but does NOT include elevation views or cross-sections showing the horizontal distance or clearance from the overhead conductors to the pond edge. No engineer-sealed profile exhibits demonstrating the 7-foot-6-inch minimum sky-to-ground clearance were found.
findings.reasoning: The detention pond is a man-made water quality feature (defined as a water quality feature under the checklist). The overhead electric line running along the eastern boundary serves distribution facilities (indicated by '-OE-' notation and transformer pads shown on Sheet 21, confirming distribution voltage, not transmission). UCM § 1.10.3 requires a minimum 7-foot-6-inch horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the pond edge to the nearest overhead distribution conductor. The site plan documents do not provide evidence of this clearance: Sheet 16's pond profiles show only the pond's internal cross-sections and elevation changes, not the clearance to the adjacent overhead line. No dimension lines, callouts, or professional engineer certification showing the measured distance between the pond boundary and the overhead conductors are present in the submitted plans. The absence of this clearance verification documentation, combined with the pond's adjacency to the overhead line, indicates non-compliance with the requirement.

findings.comment: Detention pond does not demonstrate required minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. applicableAreas: Detention pond in northeast corner relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the detention pond in the northeast corner adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 12 shows the overhead electric line (-OE-) running along that boundary in close proximity to the pond wall. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires water quality features to maintain a minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors, measured as a radius in all directions from the conductor locations. The detention pond's proximity to the overhead line on the eastern boundary suggests potential non-compliance. The submitted plans do not provide professional engineer-sealed exhibits demonstrating that the pond maintains this 15-foot radial clearance. Without such documentation, the application cannot demonstrate compliance. The presence of the pond adjacent to the overhead line, without radial clearance verification, indicates a deficiency.

findings.comment: Missing engineer-sealed profile plans or section exhibits showing clearance verification and dimensions between detention pond and overhead electric conductors. Submit professional engineer-prepared profiles showing conductor locations (all phases), pond boundary location, and horizontal/vertical clearances with dimension callouts demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 minimum clearances (7.5 feet horizontal, 15 feet radial).
applicableAreas: Detention pond near overhead electric facilities in northeast corner
findings.observation: The detention pond is positioned within 15 feet of overhead electric conductors on the eastern property boundary (confirmed by Sheet 9 showing pond position and Sheet 12 showing overhead line location). Sheets 15 and 16 contain pond design cross-sections and profiles showing internal pond elevations and sedimentation/filtration details. However, these sheets do not include professional engineer-sealed profile sections or elevation views that show: (1) the location of the overhead conductors (all phases), (2) the exact location of the pond boundary, and (3) the horizontal and vertical clearances between the pond edge and the nearest conductor with dimension callouts. No detail sections referenced in the drainage plan sheets (Sheets 15-16) are cross-referenced to sheets showing this clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that where water quality features are proposed near electric facilities (within 15 feet of overhead conductors), plans must include profile plans, engineer-scaled section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification with dimensions between water quality features and electric facilities. The requirement is explicit: applicants must demonstrate compliance through professional engineer-certified exhibits showing measured clearances. The pond profiles provided (Sheets 16 Sections A-A and B-B) show pond geometry and internal elevations but do not extend to show the overhead conductors or clearance dimensions. This deficiency requires submission of additional exhibit sheets showing the clearance verification.
